hashmap-get.why: Hashing finds the bucket directly; buckets stay short while the load factor is kept low.

heap-poll.why: Removing the minimum moves the last element to the root and sifts it down the heap's height.

heap-peek.why: The minimum is always at the root, index 0.

deque-ends.why: A circular array supports constant-time operations at both ends (addFirst is amortized).

unbalanced-bst.why: Inserting keys in sorted order makes it a chain. Balanced trees (TreeMap) keep it at O(log n).

print-jobs.why: Arrival order is first-in-first-out. A TreeMap keyed by arrival time also works, with more machinery; ordering by size changes the rule.

emergency-room.why: A heap gives the most urgent in O(log n) per change; re-sorting works but costs O(n log n) per arrival.

price-range.why: A sorted map answers range queries directly. A HashMap can only do it by checking every key.

friend-groups.why: Union-find merges and answers in near-constant amortized time. A fresh BFS per question works but repeats work.

pop-empty.why: Popping an empty stack decrements size to -1 and reads items[-1]. Check for empty first and throw a clear exception.

mutable-key.why: Keys must not change in ways that affect equals/hashCode while they're in a hash structure. Use immutable keys (records).

bfs-revisit.why: Without a seen set, a cycle feeds nodes back into the queue forever. Mark nodes when they're queued.

queue-poll.why: Queue.poll removes and returns the head, or null when the queue is empty (remove() would throw).

min-heap-order.why: Append at the end to keep the tree complete, then sift up until the heap order holds.

tree-size.why: An empty tree has no nodes; every real node adds one plus the sizes of its subtrees.

autocomplete.why: A trie walks the prefix once and finds every continuation below it. Checking every word works but scans the whole dictionary per keystroke.

lru-cache.why: The map finds entries in O(1) and the list tracks recency in O(1). A TreeMap works in O(log n); a plain HashMap has no notion of recency.

streaming-median.why: The two heaps keep the middle at their tops: O(log n) per number. Re-sorting is correct but O(n log n) each time.

course-order.why: Prerequisites form a directed graph; a topological order (Kahn's algorithm or DFS) is exactly an order that respects every edge.
